title: Finite-cover sections of locally constant pro-etale sets on a normal scheme
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Assume that every local ring of $X$ is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Assume that $F$ is locally constant: there is a pro-etale covering family $\{U_i\to X\}_i$ on each member of which $F$ is isomorphic to the constant sheaf associated to a set $S_i$, meaning the sheafification of the constant presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Assume also that $F$ is locally nonempty: there is a pro-etale covering family $\{V_j\to X\}_j$ and an element of $F(V_j)$ for every $j$.

Then there exists a finite etale surjective morphism $p:Y\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category, def-weil-surjective-morphism] such that $F(Y)\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.9 (Loc_X = Cov_X), pp. 67-68; proof of Lemma 7.4.10, p. 71 (every connected geometric covering is finite etale). Normality supplies geometric unibranchness by Stacks properties.tex Tag 0BQ3, lemma-normal-geometrically-unibranch.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-proetale-local-system-representability] to $X$ and $F$. Its locally Noetherian hypothesis is part of the assumed Noetherianity; its local-constancy hypothesis is exactly the specified covering by constant sheaves of sets. Obtain an etale $q:Z\to X$, with the unique valuation lifting property, and natural bijections $\theta_U:F(U)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_X(U,Z)$. Neither normality nor local nonemptiness is used at this stage.

The scheme $Z$ is nonempty. Indeed, choose a point $x\in X$. The covering $\{V_j\to X\}_j$ in the local-nonemptiness assumption is jointly surjective by the covering definition in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], so some $V_j$ has a point $v$ above $x$. Choose the given $s_j\in F(V_j)$. Under the bijection of [lem-a1-proetale-local-system-representability], $s_j$ gives an $X$-morphism $f_j:V_j\to Z$. Its image contains the point $z=f_j(v)$; hence $|Z|$ is nonempty.

source.place: Definition 7.3.1 and Lemma 7.3.9: translate a local section into a point of the representing geometric covering

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-normal-geometric-cover-components] to $q:Z\to X$. The base is nonempty, connected, locally Noetherian and quasi-compact by the hypotheses; its local rings are integrally closed domains by the stated normality assumption. The morphism is etale and has the required unique valuation lifting property by step 1. The cited lemma makes the connected component of $z$ into an open and closed subscheme $Y\subseteq Z$ and says that its structural morphism $p=q|_Y:Y\to X$ is finite etale and surjective. Its nonemptiness follows from $z\in Y$. Only this component is taken, even if $Z$ has infinitely many components.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 7.4.10, p. 71, applied to one connected component of the geometric covering

proof.text: The inclusion of etale $X$-schemes into the pro-etale site in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] makes $Y\to X$ a site object. The inclusion $i:Y\hookrightarrow Z$ is an element of $\operatorname{Hom}_X(Y,Z)$. The bijection $\theta_Y$ of [lem-a1-proetale-local-system-representability] therefore sends the element $\theta_Y^{-1}(i)$ of $F(Y)$ to $i$. This explicitly supplies a section, so $F(Y)\ne\varnothing$, and $p$ has all the required properties.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.9, evaluation of the representing presheaf on the selected finite etale component

proof_origin.place: Lemma 7.3.9 and proof of Lemma 7.4.10; take one nonempty connected component of the representing geometric covering

Sources checked: Bhatt–Scholze Def. 7.3.1(1),(3), Lemma 7.3.9 and its proof (pp. 66–68), and Lemma 7.4.10 and its proof (p. 71); Stacks properties.tex Tag 0BQ3 (lemma-normal-geometrically-unibranch). lem-a1-proetale-local-system-representability is the Loc_X ⊂ Cov_X half of 7.3.9: locally Noetherian is a special case of the standing hypothesis, the S_i may be arbitrary sets, and the lifting is unique for all valuation rings. lem-a1-normal-geometric-cover-components is 7.4.10 plus 0BQ3. I checked its extra conclusions myself: components are open because Z is locally Noetherian, the lifting property restricts to a component because Spec R is connected, and a finite etale component maps onto connected X because its image is open and closed. Both statements hold on small cases: Spec k, a singleton or infinite constant sheaf, Z empty, and a proper open that fails lifting. Neither new node restates the item. Steps 1 and 3 check every hypothesis against what the cited statements say. Step 2 uses joint surjectivity of pro-etale covers, which follows from the covering definition in def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, and step 4 uses the etale-in-pro-etale inclusion in def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism; both are genuinely elementary.
